subject: Copywriting
title: Mary Wells Lawrence: First Female CEO
description: Learn Mary Wells Lawrence: First Female CEO in one minute.

hook.text: Mary Wells painted Braniff International's planes pastel colors and dressed flight attendants in Pucci.

buildup.text: In 1966, she founded Wells Rich Greene and became the first woman to head a company on the New York Stock Exchange.

discovery.text: Her 'I Love New York' campaign saved the city's tourism. Created in 1977, the logo and slogan endure today.

twist.text: She was the highest-paid executive in advertising—not the highest-paid woman, the highest-paid person.

climax.text: Wells Lawrence proved that big creative ideas could come from women in an era that tried to say otherwise.

punchline.text: She painted planes and saved New York. Creativity has no ceiling.

quiz.question: What iconic campaign did Mary Wells Lawrence create?

details.summary: Mary Wells Lawrence became the first female CEO of a company listed on the New York Stock Exchange when she took Wells Rich Greene public in 1971. She was known for total brand transformations — painting Braniff Airlines planes bright colors and creating the 'I Love New York' campaign.
details.whyItMatters: Wells Lawrence proved that visionary brand thinking — transforming every customer touchpoint, not just ads — was the highest form of advertising. She broke gender barriers while doing billion-dollar work.
takeaways: She was the first female CEO of a NYSE-listed company
Her agency Wells Rich Greene did total brand overhauls, not just ads
The 'I Love New York' campaign revitalized the city's tourism industry

faq.question: What was Mary Wells Lawrence's approach to advertising?
faq.answer: She believed advertising should transform the entire brand experience, not just the messaging. For Braniff Airlines, she repainted planes, redesigned uniforms, and changed the in-flight experience. She treated the product itself as a canvas for creative expression.

faq.question: How did 'I Love New York' change tourism marketing?
faq.answer: Created in the mid-1970s when New York was near bankruptcy and plagued by crime, the campaign reframed the city as exciting and lovable. It became the most successful tourism campaign in history and spawned countless 'I Love [City]' imitators worldwide.
